bodies.periodText: About 15.9 hours; display phase is illustrative
bodies.surfaceMeaning: No resolved global surface imagery; the standard grid marks unmapped terrain.
unresolved: The released albedo FITS has no explicit observational coverage mask and contains a broad uniform baseline; that fill is not resolved imagery.
The bundled paper and PDS XML disagree on the pole and the XML calls a sub-day period an orbital period. Absolute phase is not claimed.

Published spin-period estimates differ: Buie et al. (2020) gives 15.9380 ± 0.0005 h, while the Porter archive labels 0.6632553 days as an orbital period. The panel reports only about 15.9 hours; no precision spin rate is installed.
bodies.name: Arrokoth
bodies.credit: Porter (2024), New Horizons Arrokoth shape model; NASA PDS
bodies.shapeMeaning: Released New Horizons contact-binary shape: two overlapping closed lobe meshes. Southern surface detail is constrained by flyby imagery; the unseen side is a source model estimate.
bodies.orientationMeaning: Revised pole from the bundled Porter paper Table 2. Its PDS XML gives an inconsistent earlier pole; the paper pole is used with arbitrary meridian and no precision spin-phase claim.
bodies.introduction: New Horizons explored this cold-classical Kuiper-belt contact binary in 2019. The released shape preserves both lobes; the unseen northern surface is modeled.

bodies.surfaceMeaning: No resolved global surface imagery; the standard grid marks unmapped terrain.
unresolved: Oblate versus triaxial shape and 8.8394 h versus 17.6788 h spin interpretations remain model-dependent.
The 572.5 MB supplementary archive contains lightcurves/model profiles, not a resolved surface texture; downloading it is unnecessary for the published numeric fit.
bodies.name: Quaoar
bodies.credit: Margoti et al. (2026), accepted ApJ; 36 stellar-occultation campaigns
bodies.shapeMeaning: Published 3D oblate fit: equatorial semiaxes 566.1 km and polar semiaxis 511.2 km. The fit assumes the body pole aligns with the rings. A competing triaxial interpretation is unresolved.
bodies.orientationMeaning: Pole RA 259.7°, DEC 53.4° inherits the measured ring-plane prior; arbitrary meridian. The 8.8394 h and 17.6788 h period interpretations remain model-dependent and no sidereal spin is installed.
bodies.introduction: This large Kuiper-belt object has two known rings. Its oblate shape is fitted to stellar occultations with the ring plane as a pole constraint; surface detail is unresolved.

bodies.surfaceMeaning: No resolved global surface imagery; the standard grid marks unmapped terrain.
unresolved: The Maclaurin model assumes satellite-orbit alignment; a slightly triaxial fit is also compatible.
Rotation period aliases prevent an absolute surface attitude claim.
bodies.name: Gǃkúnǁʼhòmdímà
bodies.credit: Proudfoot et al. (2026), accepted PSJ; occultation and satellite-orbit constraints
bodies.shapeMeaning: Published Maclaurin model with semiaxes 329, 329, 294 km. The satellite orbit is assumed equatorial. The source also permits a slightly triaxial fit; this smooth shape is a constrained model.
bodies.orientationMeaning: J2000 pole prior RA 20.6 ± 1.5°, DEC 46.25 ± 0.32° from satellite-orbit alignment. Arbitrary meridian; 11.05 h photometric period has aliases and is not installed as a qualified sidereal spin.
bodies.introduction: A distant dwarf-planet candidate with a measured occultation silhouette. This published spheroidal model combines the occultation with its satellite’s orbit; local terrain is unresolved.
